newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK funding curbs aimed against Taiwan - tycoon.
newsitem.headline: HK funding curbs aimed against Taiwan - tycoon.

text.p: An adviser to Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa has defended a plan to curb foreign donations to political groups by saying China's rival Taiwan has a history of influencing governments through funding.

Henry Tang, head of the Hong Kong Federation of Industry, was quoted on Wednesday as saying Tung's office lumped Taiwan in with foreign countries in its decision to curb foreign funding because Taipei had a history of influence peddling. China and Taiwan have been rivals since a civil war split them in 1949.
Tung is consulting the public on his plan to restrict the right to protest and to ban foreign donations to political groups after Britain hands back the colony to China on July 1.
Tang said the principles of the plan would still stand even though the public objected to it, according to the South China Morning Post newspaper.
"There has not been much argument over the principles listed in the consultation document," the industrialist said.
"Most controversy seems to lie in minor details like wording. We will listen to the public on these issues," Tang was quoted as saying.
The curbs proposal has sparked anger from the pro-democracy movement. British Governor Chris Patten also condemned it.
Two surveys in recent days have indicated Tung's popularity has fallen as a result of the plan.
Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.
